items.title: Teen dies by electrocution: Kerala Electricity Board issues apology, orders investigation
items.summary: The Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB) issued a public apology on Sunday, November 15 following the tragic death by electrocution of 14-year-old Junaid in Tirurangadi of Malappuram district. In the apology note, KSEB formally admitted official negligence, offered an apology to the family and ordered a detailed inquiry headed by a Chief Engineer. “The death of 14-year-old Junaid, who was electrocuted by the stay wire of an electric pole in Tirurangadi, Malappuram, is deeply heartbreaking. What happened should never have happened. We sincerely apologise to the public,” KSEB’s apology note read. Junaid was a native of Cherumukku Padinjarethara in Tirurangadi. On Sunday morning, he went to a paddy field near his house with friends to fish and watch a tractor plough the land. He touched a broken stay wire attached to an electricity pole that had come into contact with a live overhead power line. Junaid’s friends attempted to pull him away, but a nearby tractor driver intervened and stopped them from touching the live wire, saving them from a similar incident. items.title: RISE Legal India: 300 lawyers to gather in Mumbai as RSGI reveals its 2026 Resight India Law Firm Ratings
items.summary: London-based legal research and advisory firm RSGI will unveil its RISE Law Firm Ratings 2026 at the RISE Legal India conference, scheduled for November 18 at The St Regis, Mumbai. After 18 years of rating India's law firms, RSGI is asking a harder question: not just who wins the work, but who is built for what comes next. The 2026 RISE Law Firm Ratings judge Indian firms and international India practices on AI, pricing, management and talent, drawing on submissions, managing partner interviews and client feedback. According to RSGI, 85 Indian law firms submitted information for the assessment, while 36 international firms' India practices were evaluated. The exercise involved 101 interviews with managing partners and India practice heads, along with more than 650 client references. The conference, titled Evolutions in the Practice of Law , is expected to bring together around 300 delegates, including law firm partners, general counsel and legal technology executives. The opening session on reforming India's legal industry will feature former Bombay High Court judge Justice Gautam Patel , Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas Managing Partner Cyril Shroff , Boeing's Akhil Prasad and Hogan Love

items.title: #DataViz: Where does India shut down the internet?
items.summary: India saw more than 900 internet shutdowns in 15 years, which translates to a shutdown order every six days, on average, according to our analysis of data compiled by the Software Freedom Law Center (SFLC). Two in three of these were in Jammu and Kashmir, Rajasthan and Manipur. Preventive shutdowns, imposed in anticipation of an event, accounted for 70% (654) recorded incidents, while the rest were categorised as ‘reactive’. The longest shutdown in the tracker lasted 552 days in Jammu and Kashmir, where internet access was restricted from August 4, 2019, after the abrogation of Article 370, until 4G services were restored on February 6, 2021. Manipur’s statewide shutdown, imposed after violence broke out in May 2023, lasted 200 days. Recorded shutdowns fell from a peak of 136 in 2018 to 33 so far in 2026. Delhi recorded 11 internet shutdowns in 15 years, seven of them in 2026—as many as in Manipur and more than in any other state or Union territory this year. Globally, India had the most internet shutdowns of any country since 2019, according to the Internet Society’s Pulse shutdown tracker . Iraq had the second highest, followed by Syria and Sudan. items.title: Mere claim that man contacted terrorist through VPN not enough to order preventive detention: J&K High Court
items.summary: The Jammu and Kashmir High Court recently quashed preventive detention orders issued against a man in 2025 on allegations that he used an encrypted application or (Virtual Private Network) VPN to content persons with links to terrorist organisations [ Ajaz Ahmed Seh V/s Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir ]. Justice Wasim Sadiq Nargal acknowledged that the allegations were serious, but went on to note that the authorities had not produced any material to support such claims. "The mere assertion that the detenue used an encrypted application or a VPN, or remained in contact with persons alleged to be associated with terrorist organisations, cannot, without further particulars and relevant supporting material, furnish an adequate basis for curtailing personal liberty through preventive detention," the Court observed. The Court warned that a preventive detention order cannot be invoked merely by making serious allegations to bypass the procedural safeguards part of ordinary criminal law and keep a person in preventive detention when evidence as required by the law is yet to be secured. items.title: Supreme Court upholds NCLAT order to reconsider Videocon resolution plan involving over 95% haircut
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday dismissed the appeals against the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal’s (NCLAT) decision to send Twinstar Technologies’ ₹2,962 crore resolution plan for 13 Videocon group companies back to creditors for reconsideration. The plan involved a haircut exceeding 95 percent for creditors. A Bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe also affirmed the NCLAT’s power to return an approved resolution plan to the Committee of Creditors (CoC) and laid down guidelines governing the exercise of that power. “We have upheld the power of the NCLAT to send the approved resolution plan to the CoC. And for the reasons assigned by us, we have dismissed all the appeals,” the Court said while pronouncing its verdict. A detailed copy of the judgment is awaited. Justice PS Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe The case arose from Twinstar Technologies’ proposal to take over 13 Videocon group companies through the insolvency resolution process.
